title: Tenant cache thrash and anti-affinity emergency notes
content:
Purpose: working incident notes and a compact runbook for rapid containment when a Dedicated GPU pool shows SLO regressions that look like cache thrash + failed autoscale. This is an on-call-first doc; final postmortem will live elsewhere.

Incident snapshot
- First alert: 2025-11-18 15:12 UTC, pool 'pool-gamma' p95 exceeded target (observed ~2.6s, target 1.5s).
- 15:16 UTC: visible increase in 429 and allocator 5xx responses.
- 15:22 UTC: routing fallback triggered for several routes; observed broad KV cache miss increases.
- 15:35 UTC: noisy tenant identified (tenant: retail-beta) with long-context generation bursts. Throttling applied.
- 16:05 UTC: transient improvement then new tenant bursts.
- 17:10 UTC: autoscaler attempted scale-up but nodes stayed in provisioning: placement-driver rejections citing anti-affinity constraints.
- 18:00 UTC: manual mitigations landed; pool stabilized over next hour.

Key signals seen
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 jumped from baseline ~0.6/1.2/2.3s to ~0.9/2.6/6.1s.
- Errors: tenant 429 rate rose from ~0.2% to ~8% for retail-beta; allocator reported allocation timeouts/503s.
- GPU-level: average GPU util ~65-75% but node memory usage climbed and some nodes showed OOM spikes.
- Interconnect: node logs contained NVLink retry counts and transient driver warnings (nonfatal).
- KV cache: aggregate hit-rate dropped for tenants that were moved or that hit fallback variants.
- Autoscaler: scale attempts failed; placement-driver returned 'anti-affinity not satisfiable' and left new nodes in provisioning.

Short hypotheses (to validate)
1) Noisy neighbor with long-context work increased KV cache pressure and memory churn, which raised scheduler latency and led to allocation contention.
2) Strict anti-affinity constraints blocked autoscaler from adding capacity fast enough, prolonging the overloaded state.
3) NVLink/driver flakiness aggravated memory-copy latency under heavy context sizes, increasing tail latency.
4) Simultaneous fallback migrations multiplied cache cold-starts across tenants (no warm-start for fallback models).

Investigation steps performed
- Pulled trace rqs_20251118_3b9f in Jaeger and correlated heavy token loops to tenant requests.
- Enumerated pods: kubectl -n dedicated get pods -l pool=pool-gamma -o wide.
- Checked node NVLink logs: ssh node-07 'dmesg | grep -i nvlink'.
- Searched allocator logs for allocation timeouts: grep -i 'allocation' /var/log/allocator/allocator.log | tail -n 300.
- Reviewed autoscaler events: kubectl describe hpa pool-gamma-autoscaler -> placement-driver rejects.
- Snapshot of GPU memory usage saved: /opt/diag/gpu-mem-snapshot-20251118.tgz.

Immediate mitigations executed (timeline + outcomes)
- Applied tenant-level rate-limits to 'retail-beta' (reduced burst window and sustained RPS). Outcome: pool p95 dropped ~30% in ~12 minutes.
- Migrated three low-priority tenants off pool-gamma to pool-delta to reduce KV churn; median latency improved for remaining tenants but some migrated tenants saw transient p99 spikes while caches warmed.
- Temporarily relaxed placement-driver enforcement (soft-affinity allow flag) to permit autoscaler nodes to provision; autoscaler succeeded after change.
- Rebooted drivers on two hosts that presented NVLink warnings; driver restart helped partially but a node replacement was scheduled for persistent errors.

What helped vs what hurt
- Helped: targeted tenant throttling and tenant migrations bought time; relaxing placement restrictions solved the immediate provisioning blocker.
- Hurt: fallback policy caused many tenants to switch variants simultaneously, causing cache cold-start cascade; NVLink warnings persisted on one node and required hardware replacement.

Compact runbook (quick checklist for oncall)
1) Detect & scope: metrics -> filter pools where p95 > SLO. Identify top 10 tenants by tokens and RPS in last 10m.
2) Autoscaler check: kubectl describe hpa <pool-autoscaler>; look for placement-driver rejections.
3) If placement-driver rejections present and the pool is capacity-bound:
   - If safe and approved by ops owner, set placementctl flag 'soft-affinity-allow-temp' true for up to 60m to let autoscaler attach nodes. Document change in ticket and plan revert.
4) Identify suspected noisy tenants: call obs API /pools/<pool>/top-tenants?window=10m and sort by tokens.
5) Apply temporary throttles to noisy tenants: rlim-cli set-tenant-rate <tenant> --burst <b> --sustained <s>. Aim for immediate RPS reduction of ~60%.
6) If spare pools available, migrate low-priority tenants out: tenantctl migrate <tenant> --from <pool> --to <pool-alt> --maint-window 2m. Run dry-run first.
7) If NVLink/driver warnings present: mark node drain candidate, restart driver, re-run diagnostics; if warnings persist schedule replacement.
8) Monitor KV cache hit-rate and fallback churn; if we see large cache cold-start penalty, avoid triggering widespread fallbacks simultaneously and consider staggered rollout.
9) After stabilization: revert any placement-driver flags, resume normal autoscaler behavior, and log all temporary actions to incident ticket.

Quick command snippets
- Top tenants: curl -s 'https://obs.internal/api/pools/pool-gamma/top-tenants?window=10m' | jq
- Throttle tenant: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"tenant":"retail-beta","rate":20,"burst":50}' https://controlplane.internal/tenants/throttle
- Toggle placement flag: placementctl set-flag soft-affinity-allow-temp true --expires 60m --reason 'incident 2025-11-18'
- Migrate tenant fast-path: tenantctl migrate retail-alpha --from pool-gamma --to pool-delta --maint-window 2m

Post-incident follow-ups (owners & tickets)
- eng-serving-runtime: implement KV cache warm-start or lightweight state sync for fallback model variants (INF-5120).
- eng-sre: add a one-click emergency placement-driver override and improve error messages for anti-affinity rejection reasons (SRE-4321).
- infra/hardware: replace node-07 due to persistent NVLink errors and capture pre/post replacement telemetry (HW-209).
- product: adjust default fallback behavior to avoid simultaneous migrations across many tenants (PROD-98).
- observability: alert on placement-driver rejection rate > 5/min and on sudden KV cache hit-rate drops (OBS-765).

Hypotheses to validate in staging
- Reproduce autoscaler rejection with strict anti-affinity and tenant burst pattern; validate behavior when soft-affinity flag toggled.
- Measure time-to-warm for KV cache for typical fallback sequence; try pre-warm approaches.
- Correlate long-context request traces with NVLink retry counts to test whether interconnect flakiness amplifies tail latency.

Open operational questions
- Should oncall be allowed to use soft-affinity override by default? Tradeoff: faster recovery vs capacity fragmentation risk.
- Can we design a staggered fallback mechanism that warms caches before switching large numbers of tenants?
- Are there proactive signals (pattern of cache miss + small latency uptick) we can alert on earlier?

Notes and next steps
- Keep this document short and action-oriented for next oncall. Expand into full postmortem once tickets reach maturity.
- If you touch placement-driver flags during an incident, add the exact command and expiry time to the incident ticket and notify capacity owners.

End of notes.
